On 13.02.2023, following order was passed:
"Present petition is under Section 438 Cr.P.C. for seeking anticipatory bail to the
petitioner in case Fir No.29 dated 19.07.2019 registered under Sections 420/120-B
Ipc at Police Station Nri, Sas Nagara, Mohali.
Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that at the earlier instance, the petitioner was a Director of Puma Realtors Pvt. Ltd.
The petitioner had resigned from the company as back as on 24.06.2014 as is evident from the form No. DIR-12 as Annexure P-2.
The complainant had allegedly booked an apartment with the aforesaid company on 30.06.2017 and a sum to the tune of about Rs.55,00,000/- was deposited by her.

Subsequently, the company has gone into liquidation and has been Madhukar Tulsi vs State Of Punjab on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104986930/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The principal amount has been repaid to the complainant and the interest @ 8% has also been agreed to be paid to the complainant.
Notice of motion.
Ms. Ruchika Sabherwal, DAG, Punjab accepts notice on behalf of the respondent-State.
Adjourned to 11.05.2023.

Meanwhile, it is directed that in the event of arrest, the petitioner be admitted on interim bail on furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer subject to the condition that he joins the investigation and comply with other conditions as specified under Section 438(2) Cr.P.C."
1 of 2 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:074060 CRM-M-7473-2023 2023:PHHC:074060 2.
Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that in pursuance of the interim directions, the petitioner has joined the investigation.

3. Learned State counsel, on instructions from SI Amandeep Singh, has not disputed the aforesaid factual aspect and further submitted that the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not required.
4. Considering above, the petition is allowed and the interim bail granted by this Court vide order dated 13.02.2023 is made absolute.
22.05.2023 (VIVEK PURI)
